To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vast majority of VN/FN neurons responded during both rotational motion and translational motion but showed little or no modulation during OKS.

the majority of neurons in the rostral vestibular nucleus and the rostral fastigian nucleus respond during both rotational and linear motion, but only a small percentage modulates during optokinetic stimulation.

most rostral VN and FN neurons respond to both vestibular and optomotor stimuli and show a wide range of preferred directions for rotation, but only a few cells respond during OKS and show a small gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms underlying the control of posture and movement.
the neural control of gaze and head movements.
the functional properties of neurons in the macaque VN and FN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vestibular nuclei, including the rostral vestibular nucleus, are not the main site of optokinetic-ocular reflex (OKR) integration.
VN and FN neurons are not exclusively vestibular but are also responsive during OKS.
there is no evidence of optokinetic- vestibular convergence on individual VN and FN cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VN/FN neurons respond robustly to 3D motion, but their responses to OKS suppression are weak and variable.
the majority of VN/FN neurons are not modulated by eye movement-related signals, and those that are do not show strong convergence between optokinetic and vestibulo-ocular responses.
the majority of VN and FN neurons are responsive to both 3D rotation and translation but are not involved in optokinetic suppression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rostral FN and VN are not involved in the generation of optokinetic nys-tagmus.
the VN and FN are not the main sites of optokinetic- vestibular integration.
the VN and FN have a broad representation of vestibular space that is not matched by OKS.
